newsitem.title: ESTONIA: C.BANK HEAD SAYS DECISION ON CREDIT RATING MAY.
newsitem.headline: C.BANK HEAD SAYS DECISION ON CREDIT RATING MAY.

text.p: Estonia's central bank governor Vahur Kraft said on Friday a decision would be made in May by the central bank and commercial banks on whether Estonia should seek an international country credit rating.
"The central bank supports the idea by the question is for whom the credit rating is needed," Kraft told Reuters in an interview.
"Our fiscal policy is a balanced budget and monetary policy a fixed exchange rate so the government and central bank don't need a credit rating.

"But of course we understand that to have this credit rating is to join the club of countries and then you have better opportunities to get credit lines to commercial banks, to the manufacturing sector and so on.
"It is easier to go to the international capital market."
Kraft said the Bank of Estonia and the Banking Association was looking at applying for a credit rating.

"But we need to look at some problems in Estonia such as changing some of the laws to restrict borrowing of local authorities...and to control the rapid growth loan portfolios (of commercial banks)," he said.
"If we can dimimish these kinds of risks then I think we have quite a good possibility to go with the commercial banks to seek a credit rating."
He said the central bank and Banking Association had decided to meet in early May to decide finally if and when they can seek an international credit rating.
"We need to look at concrete steps to handle the process," he said.
Estonia is the last of the three Baltic countries to seek an international credit rating.
